title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README to understand tmux-rendez-vous: a TPM plugin that unifies sesh (session management) and lazy-tmux (persistence) behind a tmux popup picker.

title: Plugin Entry Point
description: plugin.tmux bootstraps the plugin: sources tmux-bash-lib, validates dependencies (tmux 3.6+, bash 4.4+, sesh, lazy-tmux, fzf), sets default options, and conditionally starts the save daemon.

title: The Picker Flow
description: rendez-vous is a thin wrapper that opens a tmux popup running rendez-vous-picker — the interactive fzf-based session browser that aggregates 4 sources (active sessions, sleeping sessions, configs, zoxide dirs).

title: Session Lifecycle
description: connect-rendez-vous handles session restoration with mutex locking, hooks, and linked windows. close-rendez-vous saves then kills sessions. list-rendez-vous queries all session sources via sesh and lazy-tmux.

title: Persistence & Save Daemon
description: save-rendez-vous persists session state via lazy-tmux with before/after hooks. rdv-saver-daemon runs periodic saves in the background using a configurable interval.

title: Window Linking & Notifications
description: verify-linked-windows (Python) manages cross-session window linking. window-linker displays a menu of linkable windows. rdv-notify provides a daemon+task notification system using a named pipe and tmux status bar.

title: Configuration & Tooling
description: Project tooling: pre-commit hooks for conventional commits and linting, cocogitto for changelog generation, ruff/pyright/rumdl for Python and markdown linting, and shellcheck for bash validation.
